sources.citation: Muniru, John, Kendall D. Decker, Yakubu Danladi, Christina Riepe, Benard Abraham, Jonah Innocent & David Onoja. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Ajiri (Eloyi) [afo] Language of Nasarawa and Benue States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-035. SIL International. 67 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 8.3 'Phonetic similarity and variation' (pp. 21-23) gives consonant and vowel inventories and says (p. 23) 'There may be five tones (low, mid, high, rising-falling, and falling-rising). A thorough tone analysis is beyond the scope of this report.' The word 'stress' does not occur in the report. downloaded from the the Internet Archive (the Internet Archive.archive.org capture 20241114065925) because sil.org is behind an automated-access block.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. Prospecting proto-Plateau. Draft ms., rogerblench.info
sources.note: Cited by Wikipedia for Eloyi's classification; general Plateau overview, unlikely to add stress information but might carry a one-line prosodic characterisation of Eloyi.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007 [Glottolog lists as 2006]. The Eloyi language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 15 September 2007. Cambridge: ms. 29 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 'Phonology' (pp. 2-3) opens 'The phonology of Eloyi remains tentative', gives a 7-vowel and consonant inventory; the subsection 3.3 'Tones' (p. 3) is a bare heading with no text under it (verified in the text; no images on the page). 'Stress' does not occur in the file. downloaded from the Internet Archive.archive.org (capture 20150420033910) because rogerblench.info is captcha-blocked.

sources.citation: Armstrong, Robert G. 1983. The Idomoid languages of the Benue and Cross River valleys. Journal of West African Languages 13(1): 91-149.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the word does not occur in the 58-page scanned). Typological remarks pp. 97-98: Igede has a four-level register tone system, 'All the other Idomoid languages have three-register systems'; downdrift rare, downstep non-existent; 'With very rare exceptions, all syllables are open. Where noun plurals are distinguished, they always have the same tones as the singular except in Eloyi. There the i-/i- animal class makes a systematic tonal difference in the plural in the Southern or Eloyi Mbeji dialect. In the Northern or Eloyi Mbekyi dialect, singular-plural tone differences occur…

sources.citation: Armstrong, Robert G. 1964. Notes on Etulo; A few more words of Eloyi. Journal of West African Languages 1(2): 57-60.
sources.note: Nothing. The Eloyi part (pp. 59-60) is a supplementary wordlist (Eloyi Mbeci dialect, from a Mr Ekute of Esaari) with tone marks and a duodecimal numeral list; the only phonology statement in the article (three tone levels) is about Etulo, not Eloyi. Scan scanned.

sources.citation: Mackay, Hugh D. 1964. A word-list of Eloyi. Journal of West African Languages 1(1): 5-12.
sources.note: Nothing. Scan scanned. 'PHONEMICS' and 'PROSODIC FEATURES' (pp. 5-6): 'Vowels occasionally occur long (marked :) or overlong (marked ::). There are three levels of tone, high, mid (but usually unmarked in this paper), and low. Very occasionally falling or rising tones occur.' Phonetic note 5: 'All final low tones have an extra low glide.' No mention of stress.
